The process begins when documents are sent to the receiving department. Upon receipt, a receiving report is created.

Following the creation of the receiving report, two activities occur simultaneously: errors are reported to the relevant team member, and a three-way match is double-checked.

Once both of these activities are completed, three tasks are initiated in parallel: a voucher is created for the documents, the documents are stored in the paid invoice file, and the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account.

After the voucher is created, two additional activities happen concurrently: dates are checked to avoid penalty charges, and the payment is scheduled.

The process concludes once all parallel activities are finished—specifically when the documents have been stored in the paid invoice file, the invoice has been entered into accounts payable, the dates have been checked, and the payment has been scheduled. At this point, the process ends.

The process begins with confirming the basic information.

Once the basic information is confirmed, two activities are carried out simultaneously: identifying the process's components and assessing the performance of the process. After the performance assessment is complete, a confirmation is made regarding whether the process requires optimization.

After both the component identification and the optimization confirmation are finished, the process continues by defining how long it takes to complete the process. Following this, potential process improvements are written, and then approval for the processing improvements is obtained.

Once approval is granted, two activities occur in parallel: using the updated process and defining what would make the improvements successful.

After both of these activities are completed, another set of parallel activities begins: communicating the process changes and scheduling the next process review and optimization. Following the communication of changes, the process changes are implemented.

Once both the implementation of changes and the scheduling of the next review are complete, the process comes to an end.

First, the ticket type is checked. Following this check, three parallel paths are initiated simultaneously.

In the first path, the ticket type is determined as a Marketing/PR Question.

In the second path, the ticket type is determined as a Technical Issue. Once identified as a technical issue, the ticket type is then determined as a Feature Request, after which the issue is replicated.

In the third path, the ticket type is determined as a Simple Question.

All three parallel paths must complete before the process can continue. Once the Marketing/PR Question determination, the issue replication (following the Technical Issue and Feature Request determinations), and the Simple Question determination are all finished, the paths converge and the process ends.

The process begins when an order is received.

First, the order details are recorded. Following this, two activities happen simultaneously: the products are checked to confirm they are in stock, and a record is made of which products were taken from storage.

After checking stock availability, the ordered products are requested from inventory. In parallel, once the storage records are updated, quality checks are performed on the products. Both of these paths must complete before proceeding.

Next, depending on the situation, one or more of the following activities may occur: the items are packaged securely, and/or approval is obtained. If approval is obtained, three activities then happen simultaneously: a packing slip is printed, the products are measured, and the shipping label is attached to the packaging. After attaching the shipping label, an invoice is printed. Once the packing slip is printed, the measurements are completed, and the invoice is printed, these parallel activities converge.

After all applicable packaging and approval-related activities are completed, the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle. Finally, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

The process begins and the first step is to record basic details about the customer.

After recording the basic details, two parallel activities are initiated simultaneously: determining ways to increase value and identifying key points of value.

Following the determination of ways to increase value, an analysis of how the customer uses the product is conducted. Meanwhile, after identifying key points of value, the impact of cancellation is quantified.

Once both the product usage analysis and the cancellation impact quantification are completed, the process continues by recording whether the customer is willing to talk.

If they are willing to engage, the root cause or causes of the problem are identified.

After identifying the root causes, three activities are carried out in parallel: describing ideas to increase value, presenting the customer with a special offer, and informing them of key metrics that demonstrate the value of the product.

Once all three of these activities are completed, the customer is thanked for their time and feedback.

Following this, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns.

Finally, important learnings from the conversation are noted down, and the process ends.

The process begins and the first step is to prepare a summary of your content.

Once the summary is prepared, two activities are initiated simultaneously: emailing your subscribers and posting on related forums and groups.

After emailing your subscribers, two more activities begin in parallel: commenting on related blog posts and deep-linking to the content from older posts.

Following the completion of commenting on related blog posts, three activities are launched concurrently: posting on Q&A sites, submitting to link roundups, and reverse engineering your competition.

These three activities—posting on Q&A sites, submitting to link roundups, and reverse engineering your competition—must all be completed before proceeding. Once all three are finished, the process waits for the deep-linking to the content from older posts to also be completed.

After both the deep-linking activity and the three concurrent activities are done, the process then waits for the posting on related forums and groups to be completed as well.

Once all parallel branches have converged—meaning emailing subscribers and its subsequent activities are finished, and posting on related forums and groups is also complete—the process comes to an end.

The process begins when a ticket is received and needs to be handled.

First, the ticket type is checked to determine how it should be processed. Based on this check, the ticket can be classified into one or more categories simultaneously, as the process allows for multiple paths to be taken.

If the ticket is identified as a 'Feature Request', it triggers two parallel activities that must both be completed: the ticket is determined as a 'Simple Question' and also as a 'Billing Question'. Once both of these determinations are finished, the process continues forward.

If the ticket is identified as an 'App Question', it is determined as such and then proceeds directly to the next stage.

If the ticket is identified as a 'Sales Question', it can lead to one or more of the following determinations: the ticket may be classified as a 'Marketing/PR Question', an 'I'm not sure question', or a 'Mixed-type question'. Any combination of these classifications may apply, and once the relevant determinations are complete, the process moves forward.

After all the applicable ticket type determinations have been made and consolidated, the process proceeds to the response phase. At this point, one or more response activities may occur: the issue may be replicated, and/or the ticket question may be responded to directly. If the ticket question is responded to, technical issues are then tested afterward.

Once all response activities are completed—whether replicating the issue, or responding to the question and testing technical issues—the process concludes and reaches its end.

After these parallel activities conclude, the loan funds are received, and the process ends.

The process begins with setting a target date for approval.

Once the target date is established, two activities are performed simultaneously: reviewing the most recent budget and evaluating any significant variances. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

After both the budget review and variance evaluation are finished, the next step is to determine ways of achieving the goals.

Following this determination, two calculations are carried out in parallel: calculating the total annual budget and estimating the average monthly cost. Both calculations must be completed before moving forward.

Once both financial calculations are done, the total annual income is projected.

After projecting the income, two activities occur simultaneously: recording the financial data in a budget spreadsheet and finalizing the budget. Both of these must be completed before continuing.

At this point, the process offers flexibility in how to proceed with one or more approval paths. One option is to request approval from top management directly. Another option is to assign management responsibilities, which then triggers two parallel activities: obtaining approval from top management and incorporating the budget into the master budget. Both of these activities must be completed if this path is taken.

The process concludes once either the direct approval request is completed, or the management responsibilities path with its subsequent approval and incorporation activities is finished, or both paths are completed if both were initiated. The process then reaches its end.

The process begins when an invoice needs to be processed.

First, the documentation is sent to the vendor accounting department. Following this, a receiving report is created.

After the receiving report is created, two activities occur simultaneously: the vendor's invoice is gathered, and a three-way match is double-checked.

While the three-way match is being verified, two additional activities happen in parallel: the receiving report is gathered, and any errors are reported to the relevant team member. Once both of these activities are completed, they synchronize with the completion of gathering the vendor's invoice.

After all these parallel activities converge, three activities begin simultaneously: dates are checked to avoid penalty charges, the documentation is stored in the paid invoice file, and the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account.

While checking dates to avoid penalty charges, two more activities occur in parallel: a voucher is created for the documents, and all documents are stamped. Once the voucher creation and document stamping are both completed, they join together with the completion of storing in the paid invoice file and entering the invoice into accounts payable.

After all these parallel streams converge, the payment is scheduled.

The process ends once the payment has been scheduled.

The process begins when a customer retention interaction is initiated.

First, the basic details of the customer are recorded, followed by identifying the key points of value that the service or product provides to this particular customer. Next, it is recorded whether or not the customer responded to the outreach, and then a summary is created documenting why they want to leave.

At this point, two activities are performed simultaneously: the customer is informed of key metrics demonstrating the value they receive, and at the same time, ideas to increase the value for the customer are described. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

Following this, depending on the circumstances, one or both of the following activities may occur: the customer's decision is recorded, and/or they are thanked for their time and feedback. At least one of these activities takes place, and once all applicable activities are completed, the process continues.

The customer is then asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, the learnings from this interaction are sent to the appropriate managers, and the process ends.

The process begins when an order is received and needs to be fulfilled.

First, payment receipt is confirmed to ensure the transaction has been completed successfully. Once payment is verified, the ordered products are requested from inventory.

At this point, two activities happen simultaneously: a shipping label is attached to the packaging, while separately, approval is obtained for the order.

After approval is secured, two tasks proceed in parallel: the products are measured, and the items are packaged securely.

While measuring the products, two additional tasks are performed concurrently: the invoice is printed and the packing slip is printed. Once both printing tasks are complete, they converge with the packaging activity.

Following the completion of both the measuring/printing activities and the secure packaging, three delivery-related tasks are carried out simultaneously: the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle, the delivery is arranged, and other orders are examined for potential delivery overlaps to optimize logistics.

Once all three delivery tasks are finished, they merge together with the shipping label attachment activity that was running in parallel from earlier in the process.

Finally, after all parallel paths have converged, a confirmation email is sent to the customer to notify them about their order status, and the process concludes.

Request the ordered products from your inventory
Attach the shipping label to the packaging
Load items into the delivery vehicle
Examine your other orders for delivery overlaps
Send a confirmation email to the customer

Once communication has been maintained and KPIs have been recorded, the project outcomes are evaluated.

The process begins with unmuting all gradebook columns.

Once this is complete, two activities are performed simultaneously: the gradebook is imported, and the grades are calculated. Both of these tasks must be finished before proceeding.

After both the gradebook import and grade calculation are complete, two review activities occur in parallel: the grades summary is reviewed, and the course summary is reviewed. Both reviews must be completed before moving forward.

Following the completion of both reviews, the final grades are exported.

After exporting the final grades, one or both of the following activities may be performed depending on the circumstances: obtaining approval signatures from the course director, and submitting the results to the SSO (Student Services Office). At least one of these activities must be completed, though both may be carried out.

Once the required approval and/or submission activities are finished, the process comes to an end.

The process begins at the start event and proceeds to check the ticket type.

After checking the ticket type, three activities are performed simultaneously in parallel: the ticket type is determined as a Technical Issue, the ticket type is determined as a Simple Question, and the ticket type is determined as a Marketing/PR Question.

Once all three ticket type determinations have been completed, the process continues with two activities occurring in parallel: the issue is replicated, and the ticket question is responded to.

After both replicating the issue and responding to the ticket question have been completed, the process concludes at the end event.

1.text:
The process begins when a support ticket is received.

First, the ticket type is checked. Following this, three activities are performed simultaneously: the ticket is evaluated to determine if it is a technical issue, assessed to see if it is a simple question, and reviewed to check if it is a marketing or PR question. All three of these determinations must be completed before proceeding.

Once all ticket type determinations are finished, two activities are carried out in parallel: the issue is replicated to understand and diagnose the problem, and the ticket question is responded to. Both of these activities must be completed before the process can conclude.

After both the issue replication and the ticket response are finished, the process ends.

The process begins when the contract is sent to the client.

Following this, three activities are initiated simultaneously: future calls are scheduled, the client's CRM is updated, and the project management profile is updated.

After scheduling future calls, one or more of the following activities may occur depending on the circumstances: approval for the first draft is obtained, or a first draft of the marketing plan is created. If the marketing plan draft is created, campaign ideas are then researched.

Meanwhile, after updating the project management profile, confirmation that the questionnaire is complete takes place.

The process waits until the client's CRM has been updated, the questionnaire completion has been confirmed, and any applicable activities from the approval or marketing plan path have been completed.

Once all these parallel activities converge, the client is informed of the project start.

After informing the client, three activities begin simultaneously: changes are made based on a follow-up call, a follow-up call is held, and a post-onboarding survey is sent.

The process concludes once all three of these final activities—making changes based on the follow-up call, having the follow-up call, and sending the post-onboarding survey—have been completed.

The process begins with recording the customer's basic details.

Following this, three activities are performed simultaneously: analyzing how the customer uses the product, determining ways to increase value for them, and identifying key points of value. Additionally, after analyzing product usage, the impact of potential cancellation is quantified. All three parallel paths must complete before proceeding.

Next, two activities occur in parallel: confirming the call date and time, and giving the customer a call. After confirming the call details, one or more of the following may happen depending on the situation: recording whether or not the customer responded, and recording if they are willing to talk. If the customer did not respond, an email is sent to them. These paths, along with the direct call activity, converge before moving forward.

The process then continues with one or both of the following activities as applicable: summarizing why the customer wants to leave, and asking open-ended questions to understand their concerns better. Once these are completed, three activities are performed simultaneously: describing ideas to increase value for the customer, presenting them with a special offer, and informing them of key metrics that demonstrate the value they receive. All three must be completed before continuing.

Following this, one or both of the following activities may occur: thanking the customer for their time and feedback, and recording the customer's decision. After these converge, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns.

Finally, important learnings from the conversation are noted down, and the process ends.

The process begins when a ticket is received.

First, the ticket type is checked to understand the nature of the inquiry. Following this, the ticket type is determined to be a 'Sales Question'.

Next, an attempt is made to replicate the issue described in the ticket. After this replication attempt, a decision is made based on whether all parties could replicate the issue.

If all could replicate the issue, the process ends at this point.

However, if not all could replicate the issue, technical issues are tested to further investigate the problem. Following the technical testing, another attempt is made to replicate the issue.

After this second replication attempt, another decision point is reached. If all could now replicate the issue, the process ends.

If not all could replicate the issue even after technical testing, the ticket question is responded to directly. After providing this response, the process concludes.

The process begins with recording basic details, followed by evaluating any significant variances.

After evaluating variances, two activities are performed simultaneously: prioritizing three to five goals and defining three to five goals. Once both of these activities are completed, the total annual budget is calculated.

Following the budget calculation, two activities occur in parallel: projecting total annual income and listing all sources of income. After both of these are finished, the budget is finalized.

Upon finalizing the budget, two parallel paths begin. On one path, management responsibilities are assigned, which then triggers two simultaneous activities: requesting approval from top management and incorporating the budget into the master budget. On the other parallel path, approval is obtained from top management.

The process concludes once all three activities—obtaining approval from top management, requesting approval from top management, and incorporating into the master budget—have been completed.

The process begins when an order is initiated. First, the team confirms that payment has been received from the customer.

Once payment confirmation is complete, three activities are carried out simultaneously: recording which products were taken from storage, performing quality checks on the items, and requesting the ordered products from inventory.

After all three of these parallel activities are finished, the process continues with two concurrent tasks: printing the packing slip and getting approval.

Once the packing slip is printed, two more activities begin in parallel: packaging the items securely and printing the invoice. After the invoice is printed, the products are measured.

The process then waits until all three activities are complete—the secure packaging, the product measurements, and the approval—before proceeding.

Once these are all finished, the team examines other orders for potential delivery overlaps. Following this review, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process comes to an end.

The process begins with recording basic details.

Once the basic details are recorded, two activities are performed simultaneously: reviewing the most recent budget and evaluating any significant variances. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

After both the budget review and variance evaluation are finished, two more activities occur in parallel: prioritizing three to five goals and defining three to five goals. The process waits until both goal-related activities are complete.

Following the completion of goal prioritization and definition, the process splits again into two concurrent paths. On one path, the average monthly cost is estimated. On the other path, the total annual budget is calculated, which is then followed by listing all department expenses. The process continues only after both the cost estimation and the expense listing are done.

Next, the total annual income is projected. Once this projection is complete, two activities are carried out simultaneously: recording financial data in a budget spreadsheet and finalizing the budget. Both must be finished before moving forward.

After the financial data is recorded and the budget is finalized, the process again branches into two parallel activities: incorporating the budget into the master budget and assigning management responsibilities. Following the assignment of management responsibilities, approval is requested from top management.

The process concludes once both the incorporation into the master budget and the approval request from top management are completed.

The process begins when a customer cancellation case is initiated.

First, the basic details of the customer and their cancellation request are recorded. Following this, the impact of the cancellation is quantified to understand its significance.

Once the impact has been assessed, three activities are carried out simultaneously: an email is sent to the customer, the call date and time are confirmed, and the customer is given a call. After sending the email, whether or not the customer responded is recorded. After calling the customer, it is recorded if they are willing to talk. These three parallel paths—recording the email response, confirming the call schedule, and recording the customer's willingness to talk—must all be completed before proceeding.

Once all three activities converge, the reasons why the customer wants to leave are summarized. Following this summary, two activities occur in parallel: ideas to increase value are described to the customer, and they are informed of key metrics demonstrating the value of the service or product.

After both the value proposition and metrics have been communicated, two more activities happen simultaneously: the customer is thanked for their time and feedback, and the customer's decision is recorded.

Once both the thank-you and the decision recording are complete, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, important learnings from the conversation are noted down, and the process comes to an end.

Inform them of key metrics demonstrating value

First, the basic details of the cancellation are recorded. Following this, the impact of the cancellation is quantified.

After quantifying the impact, two activities occur simultaneously: recording whether the customer is willing to talk, and sending them an email. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

Once both activities are finished, the root cause(s) of the problem are identified. After understanding the underlying issues, ideas to increase value are described.

At this point, depending on the circumstances, one or both of the following activities may take place: thanking the customer for their time and feedback, and recording the customer's decision. At least one of these must be completed, though both may occur.

After completing the applicable activities, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns.

Following this inquiry, two activities are initiated in parallel: sending learnings to appropriate managers, and noting down important learnings from the conversation. Both of these activities lead to the conclusion of the process.

The process ends once the learnings have been documented and shared with the relevant managers.

After testing the technical issues, that branch waits for the other parallel activity to complete. Once both the technical issue testing is complete and the replication decision path has concluded, the two parallel branches synchronize, and the process comes to an end.

The loan application process begins with the borrower submitting their ID proof to the lender.

Once the ID proof is submitted, two activities occur simultaneously: the borrower completes the loan application while the credit department receives the application. Both of these activities must be finished before the process continues.

After both the application completion and receipt are done, the credit department checks for completeness of the documentation. If the application is not complete, a written notice is given to the applicant to address the missing information. Whether the application was already complete or after the written notice has been provided, the process proceeds to the next stage.

At this point, the credit department initiates two parallel activities: they begin the underwriting process and simultaneously check the credit score and risk score of the applicant. Both of these assessments must be completed before moving forward.

Once the underwriting process and credit/risk score checks are finished, the credit department approves the loan application. Following the approval, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process comes to an end.

The process begins when a ticket is received.

First, the ticket type is checked. Following this check, three activities occur simultaneously: the ticket type is determined as 'App Question', the ticket type is determined as 'Technical Issue', and the ticket type is determined as 'Marketing/PR Question'.

When the ticket is determined to be a 'Technical Issue', two additional parallel activities are triggered: the ticket type is also determined as 'Sales Question' and as 'Mixed-type question'.

Once all the parallel ticket type determinations are complete (App Question, Marketing/PR Question, Sales Question, and Mixed-type question), the process continues to the next phase where one or more of the following activities may be executed based on the situation: testing technical issues, replicating the issue, and responding to the ticket question.

After the applicable activities from testing technical issues, replicating the issue, and responding to the ticket question have been completed, the process concludes and ends.

The process begins when a new buyer engagement is initiated.

First, the buyer's details are recorded. Once this is complete, three activities are performed simultaneously: obtaining approval for a post-credit check review, sending a credit application form to the buyer, and sending the buyer the terms of sale. After sending the terms of sale, a credit check is run on the purchasing company.

The process waits until all three parallel branches are completed—the approval is obtained, the credit application form is sent, and the credit check is finished—before proceeding.

Next, another set of three activities occurs in parallel: generating the invoice, sending the invoice through the accounting software, and checking the customer payment terms. Once all three of these tasks are completed, the process continues.

At this point, one or more recording options may be pursued. The activity may be recorded digitally, and/or a second physical copy may be made. If the activity is recorded digitally, monthly contact with the client is then established. Following this, one or both types of sales may be recorded: the sales on credit of services and/or the sales on credit of goods.

Once all selected recording activities are completed—whether digital recording leading to client contact and sales recording, making a physical copy, or both—the process concludes and ends.

The process begins by recording the basic details of a customer interaction. Following this, ways to increase value for the customer are determined.

At this point, the process splits into multiple possible paths, where one or more of the following activities may occur: recording whether or not the customer responded, giving them a call, or recording if they are willing to talk.

If the path involving recording the customer's response is taken, the process then splits into two parallel activities that must both be completed: confirming the call date and time, and sending them an email. Once both of these activities are finished, they merge back together.

After all the selected paths from the initial split converge, the root cause or causes of the problem are identified. Then, ideas to increase value are described to the customer.

The process then splits again into multiple possible paths, where one or more of the following may occur: recording the customer's decision, or thanking them for their time and feedback. Once the selected activities from this split are completed, they merge back together.

Next, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns. Following this, the process splits into two parallel activities that must both be completed simultaneously: noting down important learnings from the conversation, and sending those learnings to appropriate managers.

Once both of these parallel activities are finished, they merge together and the process comes to an end.

The customer is then asked if they have any other concerns. Following this inquiry, two final activities are performed in parallel: noting down important learnings from the conversation and sending those learnings to the appropriate managers.

The process begins with learning how to identify future failures.

After this initial step, one or more of the following activities may be performed: specifying the product market share and making plans for future products. Once the selected product-related activities are completed, the process continues.

Next, two activities are performed simultaneously: reviewing the number of employees and reviewing the business plan.

Following the business plan review, one or more of three paths may be taken: reviewing enthusiasm, reviewing team chemistry, or reviewing expertise.

If enthusiasm is reviewed, three activities are then performed in parallel: reviewing employee salary and benefits, reviewing company mission and direction, and reviewing ability as a team leader. After reviewing the ability as a team leader, two additional activities occur simultaneously: reviewing the relationship to the founder and reviewing trustworthiness. Once both of these are complete, they join back with the employee salary and benefits review and the company mission and direction review.

After all selected branches from the business plan review (enthusiasm path, team chemistry, and expertise) are completed, they converge. This convergence then synchronizes with the completion of the employee number review.

Following this synchronization, one or more financial review paths may be pursued: checking cash flow or checking exit strategy. If cash flow is checked, this is followed by checking current debt. If exit strategy is checked, this is followed by checking income statements. Once the selected financial paths are complete, the process continues to analyze the reputation of the competition.

Finally, after analyzing the competition's reputation, insurance is checked, and the process ends.

The process begins when an applicant starts a loan application.

First, the applicant fills in the employment information form. Following this, they complete the loan application.

Once the loan application is completed, two activities occur simultaneously: a written notice is given to the applicant, and the application is checked for completeness. After the written notice is given, the application is sent back to the applicant. Both of these parallel paths—sending the application back to the applicant and checking for completeness—must be finished before proceeding.

Once both activities are complete, the underwriting process begins.

After the underwriting process, three activities are carried out in parallel: the interest rate is changed, the loan application is approved, and the loan amount is reduced. All three of these activities must be completed before moving forward.

Once the interest rate change, loan approval, and loan amount reduction are all finished, the applicant receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

The process begins with preparing a summary of your content.

Once the summary is complete, two activities are initiated simultaneously: commenting on related blog posts and emailing your subscribers. These two streams run in parallel throughout the process.

In the first stream, after commenting on related blog posts, one or both of the following activities may be pursued: submitting to link roundups or reverse engineering your competition. If submitting to link roundups is chosen, two additional activities are then performed simultaneously: repurposing your content and posting on Q&A sites. After posting on Q&A sites, one or both promotional activities may be undertaken: paying for promotion or performing outreach. Once any selected promotional activities are completed, they synchronize, and then this path merges with the repurposing activity. After these activities converge, they join back with any work done on reverse engineering the competition.

In the second stream, emailing your subscribers proceeds independently.

Both the email stream and the blog post commenting stream (with all its nested activities) must complete before the process concludes and reaches its end.

The process begins with entering purchase order details, followed by creating a receiving report.

After the receiving report is created, three activities occur simultaneously: errors are reported to the relevant team member, the receiving report is gathered, and the vendor's invoice is gathered.

Once the vendor's invoice has been gathered, two activities are performed in parallel: a three-way match is double-checked, and confirmation is made that all documents have been amended.

After both the three-way match verification and the document amendment confirmation are completed, the process splits into three parallel branches. In the first branch, all documents are stamped, and then a voucher is created for the documents. In the second branch, the documents are stored in the paid invoice file, after which two activities happen concurrently: the invoice is entered into the accounts payable account, and the payment is scheduled. In the third branch, dates are checked to avoid penalty charges.

All parallel activities—creating the voucher, entering the invoice into accounts payable, scheduling the payment, checking dates, reporting errors to the relevant team member, and gathering the receiving report—must be completed before the process concludes and reaches its end.

Once this initial research is complete, two activities are performed simultaneously: considering the product necessity and specifying the product market size. Both of these product analysis activities must be completed before proceeding.

After both product-related assessments are finished, the trustworthiness is reviewed.

Following the trustworthiness review, two financial activities are conducted in parallel: checking the cash flow and checking the current debt. Both financial checks must be completed before moving forward.

Once both financial assessments are done, the process moves into competition analysis, where two activities occur simultaneously: analyzing the growth stage of competition and knowing the exact competition. Both competition-related activities must be finished before continuing.

After the competition analysis is complete, trademarks are checked.

The process concludes once the trademark check is finished.

The process begins when an order is received.

First, the order details are recorded. Once this is complete, two activities happen simultaneously: quality checks are performed on the products, and the ordered products are requested from inventory.

After both the quality checks and the inventory request are finished, three activities begin in parallel: the items are packaged securely, the products are measured, and approval is obtained.

While the packaging proceeds independently, the measurement of products triggers two additional activities that occur at the same time: the shipping label is attached to the packaging, and the packing slip is printed. Once both the shipping label attachment and packing slip printing are complete, this branch of work is finished.

After all three parallel activities are completed—the secure packaging, the labeling and packing slip preparation following measurement, and the approval—the items are loaded into the delivery vehicle.

Finally, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

First, the applicant provides the bank statement to the lender. The application is then received by the credit department for processing.

Following this, a written notice is given to the applicant acknowledging the receipt of their application. The credit department then proceeds to check the credit score and risk score of the applicant to assess their creditworthiness.

Based on the assessment, the interest rate is changed accordingly to reflect the applicant's risk profile. Finally, the applicant receives the loan funds, and the process comes to an end.

The process begins with making an introduction.

Following the introduction, three activities are initiated simultaneously: identifying the approval status, getting approval, and recording the basic idea.

The path for identifying the approval status and recording the basic idea both proceed directly toward synchronization, where they wait for other parallel activities to complete.

Meanwhile, after getting approval, the process continues by working out its value. Once the value is established, a timeline is laid out. Following this, a kickoff meeting is held, and then KPIs are recorded.

After recording the KPIs, two activities begin in parallel: evaluating project outcomes and ensuring the project is completed.

On the evaluation path, after project outcomes are evaluated, contractors are terminated. This path then proceeds to synchronize with the other parallel activities.

The path for ensuring the project is completed also proceeds toward the same synchronization point.

Once all parallel paths converge—including the earlier paths from identifying the approval status and recording the basic idea, as well as the paths from terminating contractors and ensuring project completion—the process reaches its end.

The process begins with learning how to identify future failures.

Once this is complete, two activities are carried out simultaneously: specifying the product rate of growth and making plans for future products. Both of these must be finished before proceeding.

After both activities are completed, the company mission and direction are reviewed.

Following this review, two parallel paths begin. On one path, quarterly projections are checked, and then the exit strategy is checked. On the other path, the current debt is checked, which then triggers two simultaneous activities: checking cash flow and checking income statements.

All three paths—checking the exit strategy, checking cash flow, and checking income statements—must be completed before moving forward.

Once these are done, two activities begin in parallel: knowing the exact competition and analyzing the growth stage of competition. After analyzing the growth stage, two additional activities are performed simultaneously: analyzing the reputation of competition and projecting the market share.

All three activities—knowing the exact competition, analyzing the reputation of competition, and projecting the market share—must be completed before the next step.

Finally, trademarks are checked, and the process ends.

The process begins with making an introduction to the new employee.

Following the introduction, a job description with responsibilities is provided.

After the job description is shared, one or both of the following activities may occur: the new employee may be taken out to lunch, and/or training material may be assigned. These activities can happen independently or together, depending on the circumstances.

Once the applicable activities from the previous step are completed, two activities happen simultaneously: the expectations for the following month are explained, and the first project is assigned. Both of these must be completed before proceeding.

After both explaining the expectations and assigning the first project are finished, check-in meetings are planned.

The process concludes once the check-in meetings have been planned.

The process begins with making an introduction to the new employee. Following this, a job description with responsibilities is provided, and then a tour of the office takes place.

After the office tour, three activities occur simultaneously: approval is obtained, expectations for the following month are explained, and the first project is assigned. All three of these activities must be completed before the process continues.

Once these parallel activities are finished, two more activities happen concurrently: reading material for personal growth is provided, and the new employee is encouraged to socially interact with the team. Both of these must be completed before moving forward.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee.

Following the introduction, two activities happen simultaneously: the employee's workstation is prepared, and the benefits package is prepared.

While the workstation is being prepared, the employee discusses their role, goals, and projects with their supervisor.

Concurrently, after the benefits package is prepared, two activities begin in parallel: accounts are created for the employee, and required reading materials are assigned.

Once the accounts are created, three activities proceed simultaneously: employee paperwork is prepared, a job description with responsibilities is provided, and approval is obtained.

After all three of these activities are completed—the paperwork preparation, job description provision, and approval—they converge together. This convergence point also waits for the completion of the supervisor discussion (from the workstation path) and the assignment of reading materials (from the benefits path).

Once all these parallel paths have completed, three new activities begin simultaneously: the employee is taken out to lunch, training material is assigned, and the employee is inducted into the company culture.

After the lunch, training assignment, and culture induction are all finished, three more activities proceed in parallel: the first project is assigned, approval is obtained, and the paperwork is checked.

Once the first project assignment, approval, and paperwork check are all completed, two final activities occur simultaneously: the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days, and the employee is encouraged to socially interact with the team.

After both of these final activities are completed, the process ends.

The process begins when the borrower provides the bank statement to the lender.

Following this, one or both of the following activities may occur: the application is received by the credit department, and/or the borrower completes the loan application. Once the applicable activities are completed, the process continues.

Next, two activities happen simultaneously: the application is sent back to the applicant, and a written notice is given to the applicant. Both of these must be completed before proceeding.

After both activities are finished, one or both of the following may take place: the underwriting process begins, and/or the credit score and risk score are checked. Once the relevant activities are done, the process moves forward.

Subsequently, one or both adjustments may be made: the interest rate is changed, and/or the loan amount is reduced. After any necessary adjustments are completed, the borrower receives the loan funds.

The process then ends.

Subsequently, based on the assessment results, one or both adjustments may be made: the interest rate is changed, and/or the loan amount is reduced. After at least one of these modifications is finalized, the borrower receives the loan funds.

The process concludes once the loan funds have been received.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee. Following this, the new hire discusses their role, goals, and projects with their supervisor.

After this discussion, two activities happen in parallel: training material is assigned to the new employee, and they are taken out to lunch.

Once lunch concludes, three activities occur simultaneously: a welcoming ceremony is held, expectations are explained to the new employee, and they are given a tour of the office. Following the welcoming ceremony, a mentor is assigned to the new hire. After expectations are explained, the new employee is inducted into the company culture.

Once all parallel activities are completed—the training material assignment, mentor assignment, company culture induction, and office tour—the new employee is assigned their first project.

After the first project is assigned, three activities begin in parallel: check-in meetings are planned, long-term goals are explained, and reading material for personal growth is provided. Following the planning of check-in meetings, the new employee is encouraged to socially interact with the team. After the reading material is provided, the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days.

The process concludes once all three parallel paths are complete: the encouragement to socially interact with the team, the explanation of long-term goals, and the review of the onboarding process.

The process begins with setting a target date for approval.

Once the target date is established, two activities are performed simultaneously: any significant variances are evaluated, and the most recent budget is reviewed. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

After both the variance evaluation and budget review are finished, three to five goals are prioritized. Following this prioritization, the average monthly cost is estimated.

Once the cost estimation is complete, two activities occur in parallel: all sources of income are listed, and the total annual income is projected. Both of these income-related activities must be completed before moving forward.

After listing all income sources and projecting the annual income, the financial data is recorded in a budget spreadsheet. Finally, approval is obtained from top management, and the process concludes.

The process begins when a purchase order request is initiated.

First, the basic details of the order are recorded. Once this is complete, two activities are carried out simultaneously: obtaining approval from the manager and obtaining approval from the finance team. Both approvals must be secured before the process can continue.

After both the manager and the finance team have given their approval, the supplier is informed that the order is ready for approval. Following this notification, approval is obtained from the supplier.

Once the supplier has approved, the process branches into one or more paths depending on the circumstances. The purchase order may be recorded, and details may be sent to the department. Either one or both of these activities can occur.

The process concludes once the purchase order has been recorded and/or the details have been sent to the department.

The process concludes after the customer has been notified of their order shipment.

Depending on the circumstances, either one or both of these activities will be carried out.

After the applicable closing activities are completed, the process reaches its end.

The process begins by recording the customer's basic details, followed by identifying key points of value that are relevant to the customer.

After identifying these key points, three activities occur simultaneously: an email is sent to the customer, the call date and time is confirmed, and it is recorded whether the customer is willing to talk.

Once the email is sent, two activities happen in parallel: recording whether or not the customer responded to the email, and giving the customer a call. After both of these are completed, they converge with the other parallel activities (confirming the call date and time, and recording willingness to talk).

Once all these initial outreach activities are complete, three activities are performed concurrently: asking the customer open-ended questions, summarizing why they want to leave, and identifying the root cause or causes of the problem.

After gathering this information, two activities occur simultaneously: informing the customer of key metrics that demonstrate value, and presenting them with a special offer.

Following the presentation of value and the special offer, two activities happen in parallel: thanking the customer for their time and feedback, and recording the customer's decision.

Once both of these are complete, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, the learnings from this interaction are sent to the appropriate managers, and the process ends.

After both the value demonstration and special offer have been presented, two activities occur in parallel: thanking the customer for their time and feedback, and recording the customer's decision regarding whether they will stay or leave.

Following these activities, the customer is asked if they have any other concerns. Finally, the learnings from this interaction are sent to the appropriate managers, and the process concludes.

At least one of these must be completed, though both may be done if applicable.

Once the relevant sales on credit have been recorded, the process comes to an end.

After both the credit application form has been sent and the credit check has been completed, two more activities occur in parallel: the invoice is sent in the accounting software, and the customer payment terms are checked. Again, both activities must finish before moving forward.

At this point, one or both of the following activities may be performed depending on the circumstances: recording the sales on credit of services, and recording the sales on credit of goods. The process begins with learning how to identify future failures.

Following this initial step, three activities are performed simultaneously: specifying the product market share, checking the location of the startup, and doing the SWOT analysis. After checking the location of the startup, plans for future products are made.

Once all three parallel branches are completed (specifying product market share, making plans for future products, and completing the SWOT analysis), the process continues with one or more of the following activities being performed: reviewing the number of employees, reviewing the business plan, or reviewing the company mission and direction.

After reviewing the number of employees, enthusiasm is reviewed. After reviewing the company mission and direction, two activities are performed in parallel: reviewing trustworthiness and reviewing ability as a team leader. Following the review of trustworthiness, one or both of the following may occur: reviewing team chemistry and reviewing expertise. Once these reviews are complete, they converge with the review of ability as a team leader.

When all the selected review activities are finished (reviewing enthusiasm, reviewing the business plan, and the combined reviews stemming from company mission and direction), the process proceeds to check one or both of the following: the exit strategy and the cash flow.

After these checks are completed, two activities are performed simultaneously: analyzing the reputation of the competition and knowing the exact competition. Once both of these are done, trademarks are checked, and the process concludes.

The process begins and the first step is to confirm the basic information, followed by assessing the performance of the process.

After the performance assessment, three activities are carried out simultaneously: considering where bottlenecks occur, looking to see if the process can be simplified, and defining how long it takes to complete the process.

While examining simplification opportunities, two additional activities happen in parallel: examining potentially wasteful steps and assessing if any steps are confusing. Both of these analyses must be completed before proceeding.

Once all three parallel paths are complete—the bottleneck analysis, the simplification examination (including the waste and confusion assessments), and the time definition—the potential process improvements are written.

Following this, approval for the processing improvements is obtained.

After approval is granted, two activities occur simultaneously: adding feedback on the updated process and updating the process documents. Both must be finished before moving forward.

Subsequently, three activities are performed in parallel: scheduling the next process review and optimization, determining how the process will be monitored, and communicating the process changes. The communication of changes is immediately followed by implementing the process changes.

Once the scheduling, monitoring determination, and implementation are all complete, the process ends.

The process begins with seeking pre-approval of final grades.

After obtaining pre-approval, two paths may be followed, either together or individually. On one path, the grades are calculated. On the other path, special grades are applied to individuals.

Following the grade calculation, two activities occur simultaneously: preparing grades for the Student Services Office (SSO) and selecting the exam assignment.

Once both the grade preparation and exam assignment selection are complete, two parallel activities take place: applying any changes and reviewing the course summary. After applying changes, the grades summary is reviewed.

The process then waits for both the course summary review and the grades summary review to complete, as well as for the application of special grades to individuals (if that path was taken).

Once all these activities converge, three tasks are performed in parallel: exporting the final grades, recalculating the grades, and exporting the course summary.

After all three export and recalculation tasks are finished, two final activities occur simultaneously: sending the examiners the grade approval sheet and submitting the results to the SSO.

Once both the grade approval sheet has been sent to examiners and the results have been submitted to the SSO, the process comes to an end.

Once the summary is complete, two parallel paths are initiated simultaneously. On one path, the content is posted on Q&A sites, and following that, it is submitted to link roundups. On the other path, the content is deep-linked from older posts.

After deep-linking is complete, two additional activities occur in parallel: subscribers are emailed about the content, and payment is made for promotion. Both of these activities must be completed before this path can proceed.

The process concludes only after both parallel paths have finished—that is, when the submission to link roundups is complete and when both emailing subscribers and paying for promotion have been completed. At that point, the process ends.

The process begins with recording basic details. Following this, the most recent budget is reviewed to understand the current financial situation.

Next, three to five goals are prioritized to establish clear objectives for the upcoming period. Once the goals are set, the average monthly cost is estimated to understand the expected expenses.

After estimating costs, the total annual income is projected to forecast the expected revenue. With both cost and income projections complete, the budget is finalized.

Once the budget is finalized, two activities occur simultaneously: approval is requested from top management, and management responsibilities are assigned. Both of these activities must be completed before the process concludes.

The process ends after both the approval request and the assignment of management responsibilities have been completed.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee.

Following the introduction, two activities occur simultaneously: providing a job description with responsibilities and preparing the employee's workstation. Both of these must be completed before proceeding.

Once the job description has been provided and the workstation is ready, two more activities happen in parallel: assigning a mentor to the new employee and taking them out to lunch. Both activities must be finished before moving forward.

After the mentor has been assigned and lunch has taken place, two additional activities are carried out concurrently: getting approval and assigning the first project to the employee. Both of these need to be completed before continuing.

Once approval has been obtained and the first project has been assigned, two final parallel activities begin: encouraging the new employee to socially interact with the team and providing reading material for personal growth. Both of these must be completed before the next step.

After the employee has been encouraged to interact socially and has received reading material, the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days.

The process concludes once the onboarding review is complete.

Once the buyer's details have been recorded, three activities are performed simultaneously: getting approval for a post-credit check review, running a credit check on the purchasing company, and sending the buyer the terms of sale.

After all three of these activities have been completed, the process continues with two parallel activities: sending the invoice in the accounting software and checking the customer payment terms.

Once both the invoice has been sent and the payment terms have been checked, three more activities are carried out in parallel: recording the activity digitally, making a second physical copy, and establishing monthly contact with the client.

After all three of these activities are finished, the final stage involves two simultaneous activities: recording the sales on credit of services and recording the sales on credit of goods.

Once both sales records have been completed, the process comes to an end.

The process begins when an applicant starts the loan application procedure.

First, the applicant fills in the employment information form. Once this is completed, two activities occur simultaneously: the applicant completes the loan application while the receiving party receives the application.

After both of these parallel activities are finished, one or both of the following may occur depending on the circumstances: the application is sent back to the applicant, and/or a written notice is given to the applicant.

Once the applicable notification activities are completed, the process continues with two activities happening in parallel: the underwriting process begins, and the credit score and risk score are checked.

After both the underwriting process and the credit/risk score check are completed, two more activities proceed simultaneously: the interest rate is changed, and the loan application is approved. Following the interest rate change, the loan amount is reduced.

Once both the loan amount reduction and the loan approval are complete, the applicant receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

After this initial learning phase, two parallel paths are initiated simultaneously. The first path involves specifying the product market share, while the second path focuses on specifying the product rate of growth.

Once all three of these activities are completed, they converge and two new parallel paths begin.

One path involves reviewing expertise. The other path starts with reviewing the business plan, followed by reviewing team chemistry. After the team chemistry review, two activities are performed simultaneously: checking cash flow and checking the exit strategy. These two activities then converge once both are completed.

At this point, four paths must all complete before proceeding: the product market share specification from the earlier branch, the expertise review, and the combined results from the cash flow and exit strategy checks. Once all these parallel activities have concluded, the process continues with projecting the market share.

Following the market share projection, patents are checked, and the process then reaches its end.

The process begins when an order is initiated.

First, the payment receipt is confirmed. Once payment confirmation is complete, two activities are performed simultaneously: the ordered products are requested from inventory, and a check is made to ensure the products are in stock.

After both the inventory request and stock verification are completed, the process continues with two more activities happening in parallel: the items are packaged securely, and the invoice is printed.

Once the packaging and invoice printing are both finished, the process proceeds with another set of parallel activities: other orders are examined for potential delivery overlaps, and the delivery is arranged.

After both the delivery overlap examination and delivery arrangement are completed, a confirmation email is sent to the customer.

The process concludes once the confirmation email has been sent.

The process begins by setting a target date for approval.

Following this, one or both of the following activities may occur: evaluating any significant variances and reviewing the most recent budget. At least one of these must be completed before proceeding.

Once the applicable review activities are finished, two activities are performed simultaneously: defining three to five goals, and determining ways of achieving the goals. The latter activity is followed by prioritizing three to five goals. Both paths must complete before continuing.

Next, one or both of the following calculations may take place: calculating the total annual budget and estimating the average monthly cost. After the selected calculations are done, the total annual income is projected.

Subsequently, one or both of these activities may occur: finalizing the budget and recording financial data in a budget spreadsheet. Once the applicable activities are completed, three activities begin in parallel: obtaining approval from top management, requesting approval from top management, and a third path. After obtaining approval from top management, two additional activities run simultaneously: assigning management responsibilities and incorporating into the master budget.

All three parallel paths—requesting approval from top management, assigning management responsibilities, and incorporating into the master budget—must complete before the process ends.

The process begins with recording basic details.

Once the basic details are recorded, two activities are performed simultaneously: evaluating any significant variances and reviewing the most recent budget. Both of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

After both the variance evaluation and budget review are finished, three to five goals are prioritized.

Following the prioritization of goals, one or both of the following activities may be performed depending on the circumstances: estimating the average monthly cost and calculating the total annual budget. At least one of these must be completed, though both may be done.

Once the necessary cost estimation and budget calculation activities are complete, all sources of income are listed.

After listing the income sources, two activities are carried out in parallel: finalizing the budget and recording financial data in a budget spreadsheet. Both of these must be completed before moving forward.

When both the budget finalization and data recording are done, two final activities are performed simultaneously: assigning management responsibilities and requesting approval from top management.

Once both the management responsibilities have been assigned and approval has been requested from top management, the process comes to an end.

The process begins with learning how to identify future failures, followed by specifying product details.

After the product details are specified, the process branches into a team review phase where one or more of the following activities may occur: reviewing team chemistry, reviewing ability as a team leader, and reviewing the number of employees. Once the selected team review activities are completed, the process continues.

Next, the process enters a financial review phase where one or more of the following activities may be performed: checking cash flow, checking income statements, and checking the exit strategy. When income statements are checked, this triggers two activities that must both be completed: checking current debt and checking quarterly projections. After both of these are finished, they rejoin the financial review. Once all selected financial review activities are completed, the process moves forward.

The process then proceeds to a market analysis phase where one or more paths may be taken. One path involves projecting the market share, which is then followed by identifying the exact competition. Another path involves analyzing the reputation of the competition, which is then followed by analyzing the growth stage of the competition. After the selected market analysis activities and their subsequent steps are completed, the process continues.

Finally, the process enters a final checks phase where one or more of the following may be performed: checking insurance and checking patents. Once the selected final checks are completed, the process ends.

The process begins when a borrower initiates a loan application.

First, the borrower submits their ID proof to the lender. Following this submission, two activities occur simultaneously: the credit department receives the application, and the borrower completes the loan application. Both of these activities must be finished before the process continues.

Once both the application receipt and completion are done, two more activities happen in parallel: the application is checked for completeness, and at the same time, the application is sent back to the applicant (presumably for any corrections or additional information needed). Both of these activities must conclude before proceeding.

After the completeness check and the communication with the applicant are finished, the underwriting process begins and the credit score and risk score are checked concurrently. Both assessments must be completed before moving forward.

Once the underwriting and credit evaluation are complete, two activities occur simultaneously: the loan application is approved, and the loan amount is reduced (likely based on the risk assessment findings). Both of these decisions must be finalized before continuing.

After the approval and any loan amount adjustments are made, the borrower receives the loan funds, and the process ends.

The process begins when an order is received.

First, the order details are recorded. Once this is complete, two activities are performed simultaneously: quality checks are performed, and a record is made of which products were taken from storage.

Following the quality checks, two additional activities begin in parallel: checking that the products are in stock and requesting the ordered products from inventory. These two activities, along with the recording of products taken from storage, must all be completed before the process continues.

Once all three activities are finished, two tasks are initiated concurrently: printing the packing slip and printing the invoice.

After the packing slip is printed, three activities begin simultaneously: getting approval, packaging the items securely, and measuring the products. These three activities, together with the invoice printing, must all be completed before proceeding.

Following the completion of these tasks, one or more of the following activities may be performed depending on the circumstances: loading items into the delivery vehicle, arranging the delivery, and examining other orders for delivery overlaps. Any combination of these activities that are started must be completed before moving forward.

Once the applicable delivery-related activities are finished, a confirmation email is sent to the customer, and the process ends.

Once both sales records have been captured, the process comes to an end.

The process begins with making an introduction for the new employee.

Following the introduction, two activities occur simultaneously: accounts are created for the new employee, and approval is obtained. Both of these must be completed before proceeding.

Once the accounts are created and approval is secured, three activities begin in parallel: the new employee is given a tour of the office, a welcoming ceremony is held, and a mentor is assigned.

After a mentor is assigned, three additional activities happen concurrently: expectations are explained to the new employee, they are inducted into the company culture, and training material is assigned. All three of these mentor-related activities must be completed before moving forward.

The process waits until the office tour, the welcoming ceremony, and all mentor-related activities are finished before continuing.

Next, two activities occur simultaneously: approval is obtained and the paperwork is checked. Both must be completed before proceeding.

Following this, one or more of the following activities may take place depending on the circumstances: long-term goals are explained to the new employee, the onboarding process is reviewed over the next 60 days, and the new employee is encouraged to socially interact with the team.

Once the applicable final activities are completed, the process comes to an end.

Once the basic information is confirmed, two activities occur simultaneously: confirming if the process requires optimization and identifying the process's components. Both of these must be completed before moving forward.

After these parallel activities are finished, the process continues with one or more assessment paths. One path involves assessing if any steps are confusing, while another path involves considering where bottlenecks occur.

If the confusing steps assessment is performed, two activities then happen in parallel: defining how long it takes to complete the process and looking to see if the process can be simplified. Both of these must be completed before continuing on this path.
